# [Neil’s Newsletter](/)

# FOMC Minutes - From Jan 2026 meeting

### Fed minutes confirm a committee on hold until we see more downside to inflation or employment, but "several" members considering rate hikes if inflation doesn't improve

![Neil Sethi's avatar](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!kVi2!,w_36,h_36,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fbucketeer-e05bbc84-baa3-437e-9518-adb32be77984.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fa823e9c5-392b-41ff-837b-6817250ebabc_400x400.jpeg)

Initial read of the **the** #FOMC **minutes of the December meeting come across mostly as I expected, but at the margin more hawkish.** As a reminder, in the Week Ahead (and last night) I said:

I don’t expect them to show anything different than what we already know, which is that there are a few who want cuts now, a few who don’t want cuts unless the labor market deteriorates significantly, and the majority that are willing to cut but only once inflation starts moving closer to 2%.

But **the headline takeaway (at least from BBG, WSJ, etc.), is that “[s]everal participants indicated that they would have supported a two-sided description of the committee’s future interest-rate decisions, reflecting the possibility that upward adjustments** **to the target range for the federal funds rate could be appropriate if inflation remains at above-target levels**.”

As noted, I expected a “few” who might say something like that, but not “several”. **In that regard, it is useful to consult the “quantitative table” published by the Fed in 2017** below to get a better grip on what they were intending to communicate (also, **as a reminder, the minutes are not intended as a verbatim summary** but convey a description of what the Fed wants to highlight from the meeting).

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!jwEP!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fba7a9307-10d7-46ba-9789-182e1980d7cb_761x324.png)

So as you can see, **“several” is more than “few” which means at least four and perhaps five or six officials have rate hikes as a real possibility**, and not just if inflation moves higher but if it just “remains at above-target levels”. We know that regional Fed presidents Hammack and Logan would support rate hikes but I would guess we can now add Schmidt for sure and then a couple of others (Kashkari? Bostic? Musalem? Maybe even Gov Barr?).

And **“some” (which is more than several) “commented that it would likely be appropriate to hold the policy rate steady for some time** as the Committee carefully assesses incoming data, and **a number of these participants judged that additional policy easing may not be warranted until there was clear indication that the progress of disinflation was firmly back on track**.”

In that regard, “**members agreed that inflation remained somewhat elevated…. Almost all members no longer judged that downside risks to employment had risen in recent months**.”

Although “most participants noted that **downside risks to the labor market remained**.”

In further support of my thinking that there won’t be any further rate cuts if the labor market holds up until inflation is appreciably closer to 2% are statements like these:

**“Most participants…cautioned that progress toward the Committee’s 2 percent objective might be slower and more uneven than generally expected and judged that the risk of inflation running persistently above the Committee’s objective was meaningful.** Some of these participants cited reports from business contacts who expected to increase prices this year in response to cost pressures, including those related to tariffs.

**“Several participants also raised the possibility that sustained demand pressures could keep inflation elevated** relative to the Committee’s 2 percent objective.

**“Several participants cautioned that easing policy further in the context of elevated inflation readings could be misinterpreted as implying diminished policymaker commitment** to the 2% inflation objective.

**“Most participant**s noted that recent data readings such as those for the unemployment rate, layoffs, and job openings suggested that **labor market conditions may be stabilizing** after a period of gradual cooling.

**“The vast majority of participants judged that labor market conditions had been showing some signs of stabilization** a**nd that downside risks to the labor market had diminished**.

“Participants observed that **economic activity appeared to be expanding at a solid pace.** Participants generally noted that consumer spending had been resilient, importantly supported by gains in household wealth.

“Participants observed that **business fixed investment remained robust,** particularly in the technology sector.

“**Participants generally anticipated that the pace of economic growth would remain solid in 2026**, though uncertainty about the outlook for growth remained high.

“Those who favored maintaining the target range generally viewed that, after the 75 basis point lowering of the target range last year, **the current stance of monetary policy was within the range of estimates of the neutral level.** They commented that maintaining the current target range of the federal funds rate at this meeting would leave policymakers well positioned to determine the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the policy rate.”

In addition, the minutes noted that **the Fed staff upgraded their growth and inflation forecasts** further adding to reasons to hold rates:

“The staff projection for economic activity was stronger than the one prepared for the December meeting, reflecting incoming data, greater expected support from financial conditions, and a small upward revision to the projected path of potential output. **Real GDP growth was expected to outpace potential growth through 2028 as the drag from higher tariffs waned and as fiscal policy and financial market conditions continued to support spending. As a result, the unemployment rate was expected to decline gradually starting this year,** moving below the staff’s estimate of its natural rate by the end of the year and remaining below the natural rate through 2028.”

“The staff’s inflation forecast was slightly higher, on balance, than the one prepared for the December meeting, **reflecting the expectation that resource utilization would be tighter and the path of core import prices would be higher than previously projected.”**

**Another thing I was interested in is how many participants are on board with the “1990s redux”** **concept** espoused by several Fed members (such as Powell, Paulsen, Daly, etc.) that strong growth is not a reason to leave rates higher as it may reflect strong AI-fueled productivity. It appears the answer is “several”, not as many as I would have thought:

“**Several participants also expected higher productivity growth associated with technological or regulatory developments to put downward pressure on inflation.”**

And in terms of those still concerned about the labor market it appears it is “some” which is likely around 6 to 8:

**“Some participants, however, noted that even though the labor market was showing signs of stabilization, some indicators such as survey measures of job availability and the share of those working part time for economic reasons continued to suggest softening of conditions**.”

# Range-Bound Under Pressure

Bitcoin has broken below the True Market Mean (~$79k), entering a defensive range between $79k and the Realized Price (~$54.9k). Spot flows and ETF demand remain weak, accumulation is fragile, and options positioning shows panic hedging fading, but not renewed bullish conviction.

![CryptoVizArt](/content/images/size/w100/2022/03/E4D5E3B0-8E54-4E1A-AFBA-C94B5521E2E0.jpeg)
![Chris Beamish](/content/images/size/w100/2025/09/ChatGPT-Image-Mar-27--2025--09_53_20-AM.png)
![Antoine Colpaert](/content/images/size/w100/2025/09/Profile_Pic-1.jpg)
![Glassnode](/content/images/size/w100/2019/07/500px-square-1.png)

#### [CryptoVizArt](/author/cryptovizart/), [Chris Beamish](/author/chris-beamish/), [Antoine Colpaert](/author/antoine/), [Glassnode](/author/glassnode/)

![Range-Bound Under Pressure](/content/images/size/w1000/format/webp/2026/02/woc-06-cover-4.png)

## **Executive Summary**

This report is also available for download in PDF format.

## On-chain Insights

### Defining the Bear Market Range

The market’s renewed contraction phase began in late January, marked by a decisive break below the True Market Mean, a core on-chain price model tracking the aggregate cost basis of active supply, currently positioned near $79k. Historically, deeper bear market phases have found their lower structural boundary around the Realized Price, which estimates the average acquisition cost of all circulating coins and now stands near $54.9k.

In prior cycles, these two valuation anchors have framed extended periods of compression and absorption. **In the absence of an unexpected macro catalyst, the $79k True Market Mean and the $54.9k Realized Price are likely to define the primary resistance and support corridor for the mid-term market structure.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/glassnode-studio_risk-indicator-realized-price-true-market-mean-active-investor-mean-sth-realized-price-1-.png)

### Demand Cluster Absorbing Pressure

A closer inspection of price behavior since the breakdown below the True Market Mean indicates that downside pressure has largely been absorbed within a dense demand zone between $60k and $69k. This cluster was primarily established during the H1 2024 consolidation phase, where investors accumulated within a prolonged range and have since held their positions for over a year.

The positioning of this cohort near breakeven levels appears to have moderated incremental sell pressure, contributing to the development of another sideways structure since late January 2026. **The defense of the $60k–$69k range suggests that medium-term holders remain resilient, allowing the market to transition from impulsive decline into range-bound absorption.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/glassnode-studio_btc-long-term-holder-cost-basis-distribution-heatmap-1-.png)

### Buyer Aggression in Focus

The duration of the current range-bound structure will largely depend on the strength and persistence of buy-side activity. To quantify this behavior, we examine the Accumulation Trend Score (ATS), which measures balance changes across wallet cohorts, assigning greater weight to larger entities.

The 7-day moving average of ATS reflects a notable behavioral shift, moving from strong distribution following the loss of the True Market Mean (ATS < 0.1) toward a more neutral and fragile equilibrium near 0.43. This moderation suggests that aggressive selling has eased, but conviction-driven accumulation has yet to fully re-emerge.

**A sustained rise in ATS toward 1 would signal renewed large-entity accumulation, potentially extending the current range, whereas a failure to strengthen would reinforce underlying structural fragility.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/glassnode-studio_btc-accumulation-trend-score-7d-moving-average-1-.png)

### **Liquidity Remains Constrained**

Beyond the absence of strong accumulation, broader liquidity conditions continue to reflect structural weakness. As a proxy for market liquidity, the Realized Profit/Loss Ratio provides insight into capital flow dynamics by measuring the average USD value of realized profit for every dollar realized in loss.

The 90-day moving average of this metric has been declining back into the 1–2 range, a zone that historically characterizes transitions from early bear phases toward more stressed conditions, where realized losses begin to dominate (Realized P/L Ratio < 1). This compression indicates that profit-taking remains subdued and capital rotation is limited.

**Until the Realized Profit/Loss Ratio decisively reclaims levels above 2, signalling renewed profitability and stronger liquidity inflows, the broader market bias is likely to remain structurally negative.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/glassnode-studio_btc-realized-profit-loss-ratio-90d-moving-average-1-.png)

## Off-Chain Insights

### ETFs are Still Seeing Outflows

Demand across US Spot ETFs has deteriorated materially, with the 7-day moving average of net flows rotating back into persistent outflows as BTC retraces toward the $70K region. What previously acted as a steady structural bid has now softened, signalling a contraction in marginal institutional demand.

This marks a notable shift from the prior expansionary regime, where consistent inflows helped absorb supply and support higher price discovery. Instead, flows are now broadly negative, reinforcing the view that capital allocators are stepping back rather than deploying into weakness.

**With ETF demand no longer providing a reliable cushion beneath the market, downside risk remains elevated, and any recovery attempts are likely to struggle unless netflows stabilize and re-accelerate into sustained inflows.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/glassnode-studio_btc-us-spot-etf-net-flows-btc-7d-moving-average.png)

### Spot Bias Turns Firmly Negative

Spot Cumulative Volume Delta across major exchanges has rolled over sharply, with both Binance and the broader all-exchange CVD bias flipping decisively negative. This shift reflects an acceleration in aggressive sell-side activity, as market orders increasingly lift bids rather than offers.

Notably, Coinbase spot CVD has also softened, signalling that US-based demand is no longer providing a consistent counterbalance to global sell pressure. The alignment of negative CVD across venues suggests that recent weakness is driven by active distribution rather than passive liquidity gaps.

**With spot flows skewed toward sell aggression, price action remains vulnerable. A stabilization in CVD, particularly a constructive divergence between price and spot delta, would be required to signal that organic demand is beginning to absorb supply more effectively.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/glassnode-studio_spot-indicator-cumulative-volume-delta-bias.png)

### Perpetual Funding Still Defensive

Perpetual funding rates have compressed sharply across venues, with the heatmap showing a broad shift from sustained positive funding during the advance toward $120K to increasingly neutral and negative prints as price retraces toward $70K. This transition reflects a meaningful unwind in long-side positioning.

Earlier expansion phases were characterised by persistent positive funding, signalling aggressive long leverage and trend reinforcement. In contrast, the current regime is marked by episodic negative funding spikes, suggesting traders are either hedging downside exposure or positioning tactically short into weakness.

With leverage no longer structurally skewed long, the derivatives complex has shifted into a more defensive posture. **A sustained recovery would likely require funding to stabilize alongside renewed spot demand, rather than relying solely on short-covering flows.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/funding_rate_heatmap--2-.png)

### Panic Premium Is Resetting

One-month ATM implied volatility has compressed sharply from recent panic highs, which reached 80% for the one-month tenor and 65% for the three-month, to roughly 47% across both maturities.

That decline reflects a meaningful reduction in immediate downside hedging demand. During the liquidation phase, traders aggressively paid up for short-term protection. That urgency has now faded.

The volatility risk premium is being unwound as defensive positioning is reduced. The market is no longer pricing an imminent crash scenario and instead reflects expectations of consolidation, with volatility contained within a narrower range.

This does not imply renewed bullish conviction. Rather, it signals that stress pricing has normalized and that positioning is being reset. **The takeaway is structural. The forced hedging phase appears to be behind us, and volatility expectations are recalibrating lower as market positioning stabilizes.**

![](https://insights.glassnode.com/content/images/2026/02/glassnode-studio_btc-options-atm-implied-volatility-deribit-1-.png)

### Extreme Downside Skew Eases

The 25-delta skew, which measures the volatility differential between downside puts and upside calls, has compressed meaningfully. A positive reading indicates that puts are priced richer than calls, signaling stronger demand for downside protection.

Following the retest of the $60K region, skew held near 20%. It has since eased to roughly 11% across tenors, marking a sharp 9-point moderation over recent sessions.

At the lows, puts traded at a significant premium as traders rushed to secure crash protection. That urgency has subsided. However, skew remains elevated relative to pre-selloff levels, indicating that downside hedging is still favored over upside exposure.

By 2026, the global financial system has transformed dramatically with blockchain technology moving from experimental use cases to a true foundation for institutional finance. Driving this shift are major regulations such as the **GENIUS Act** in the United States and the robust **MiCA** regulatory framework in Europe. Venture capital (VC) firms—once primarily speculation-driven and narrative-focused—now invest strategically in projects with real utility and long-term impact. They are building the backbone of decentralized physical networks (DePIN), real-world asset (RWA) tokenization, and AI-powered finance. For everyday investors and professionals alike, tracking VC capital flows has become the clearest indicator of where the blockchain industry is headed and which trends are likely here to stay.

## Top Blockchain VC Firms in 2026: Who Shapes the Future?

The leading crypto venture capital firms today are highly specialized and manage billions of dollars, with a laser focus on infrastructure, scalability, and interoperability. In this new era, the most influential players are grouped into "The Titan Tier"—including **a16z crypto**, **Paradigm**, and **Pantera Capital**. These VCs provide far more than funding: they offer regulatory advice, technical guidance, and often hands-on development support, giving their portfolio companies an edge in a highly competitive market.

### 1. The Titan Tier: Industry Trailblazers

**Andreessen Horowitz (a16z crypto)** remains the dominant force in crypto venture backed by over $40 billion in dedicated assets. Their investments cover everything from core Layer 1 blockchains to cutting-edge AI/blockchain integrations, and their latest focus is “Verifiable Compute”—ensuring that on-chain AI is both secure and transparent.  
  
**Paradigm**, founded by Coinbase co-founder Fred Ehrsam, leads with deep technical and engineering involvement. They’re known for their direct code contributions and hands-on approach. In 2026, they are the leading investor in ultra-fast blockchain networks capable of handling millions of transactions each second—matching the throughput of traditional financial players like Visa.  
  
**Polychain Capital** has established itself as the go-to fund for projects building decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN). By funding teams working on things like community-driven wireless networks and energy grids, Polychain is driving real-world adoption beyond just digital assets.

### 2. Institutional and Exchange-Backed Venture Arms: The New Accelerators

Centralized exchanges have matured beyond simple trading platforms: they now play a vital role as launchpads for promising blockchain projects.

**Coinbase Ventures** invests heavily in projects that further stablecoin adoption and institutional crypto solutions, using Coinbase’s established user base to propel new ventures to market quickly.  
  
**Galaxy Digital** focuses on bridging Wall Street and blockchain. Its current interests include making Bitcoin programmable, backing projects that bring DeFi and smart contracts onto Bitcoin’s secure network.  
  
**YZi Labs (formerly Binance Labs)** is now a global leader in developing the next generation of blockchain-powered games and social apps. Their focus in 2026 is long-term user engagement rather than short-term hype.

| **Paradigm** | High-Performance Infrastructure | $10B+ | Parallel Execution, MEV Research |

This table highlights the range of investment philosophies: a16z is leading in AI/crypto fusion, Pantera is doubling down on Bitcoin’s potential, while Paradigm is shaping the next generation of blockchain scalability and efficiency. This shows that blockchain investment in 2026 is highly specialized, with each VC fund focusing where it believes the biggest opportunities lie.

### 4. Why Exchanges Matter More Than Ever in 2026

Not all crypto exchanges are equal. The role of exchanges has evolved, and today, top-tier trading platforms serve as essential liquidity providers and even partners in project development. Gone are the days when a flashy whitepaper could win investors—modern VCs now require a proven minimum viable product (MVP) and clear on-chain data before they consider funding.

In today’s fast-paced world, mainstream media often amplifies doom-and-gloom narratives about the housing market, stirring up unnecessary anxiety among potential home buyers. Headlines scream about skyrocketing prices, economic uncertainty, and the perils of committing to a mortgage, leaving many people paralyzed by fear. But let’s cut through the noise: interest rates have dipped significantly, making this a prime opportunity for savvy buyers in Southeast Pennsylvania. As local real estate experts John and Kymberlie from The JK Team know all too well, people have been successfully purchasing homes through far tougher times—like wars, recessions, and sky-high interest rates in the past. Yet, social media and sensationalist reporting keep fueling a cycle of dread, convincing folks that waiting is always the safer bet. Drawing from alternative perspectives, we’ll explore how to ignore this fear mongering, why now is a great time to buy, and practical steps for home buyers and sellers in areas like Philadelphia suburbs, Bucks County, Montgomery County, and beyond.

## The Reality Behind Media-Driven Housing Anxiety

Fear sells—and that’s no secret in the media landscape. Independent analyses highlight how sensationalism drives clicks and revenue, often at the expense of balanced reporting. For instance, during past crises, media outlets capitalized on panic, algorithmically selling ad space tied to fear-laden content. Similarly, in the housing realm, exaggerated stories about market crashes or unaffordability create a “doomsday” vibe that doesn’t align with facts. Precarious workers interviewed during the COVID-19 era expressed distrust in media for hyping “zombie apocalypse” scenarios, seeing it as profit-driven hype rather than helpful info. On platforms like Reddit, users call out constant scaremongering around house prices, noting how it subtly manipulates public perception.

Adding to this dynamic, big corporate firms and institutional investors have been purchasing real estate across the country, often converting single-family homes into rentals. While their overall national share remains small (typically under 1% of single-family homes, per various independent research), concentrated activity in certain markets can reduce inventory for individual buyers. Alternative views suggest the persistent fear mongering—portraying the market as hopelessly out of reach—may actually benefit these large players. By keeping everyday buyers anxious and hesitant, the narrative discourages competition, allowing corporations to scoop up more properties with less pushback from motivated individuals. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle: media amplifies scarcity fears, people delay purchases, and corporate accumulation continues unchecked in targeted areas.

Social media amplifies this, turning isolated opinions into viral anxiety. Posts discuss how corporate media fosters hysteria around overheated markets, portraying buyers as “victims” while ignoring long-term benefits. Another thread points to gaslighting, where concerns about affordability are dismissed as overreactions, leaving people in perpetual worry. The result? A culture of fear that keeps potential buyers on the sidelines, missing out on opportunities in vibrant regions like Southeast Pennsylvania.

## Historical Proof: Homes Have Been Bought in Far Worse Conditions

History shows that waiting for “perfect” conditions is a myth. People bought homes during World War II, the Vietnam War era, and even the stagflation of the 1970s when interest rates soared above 18%. In the 1980s and early 1990s, amid recessions and high rates, home price appreciation slowed but didn’t reverse until full-blown economic downturns hit—and even then, nominal prices held steady in many areas. Fast-forward to recent times: Despite rates climbing post-pandemic, alternative views emphasize that high-interest environments often mean less competition, allowing buyers to negotiate better deals without bidding wars.

Today, with mortgage rates hovering around 6% (down from peaks over 7% just a year ago), the landscape is even more favorable. Experts from non-traditional sources argue that buying now locks in value before potential future hikes, especially as wage growth and economic stability support long-term appreciation. In Southeast Pennsylvania, where inventory is improving in counties like Chester and Delaware, this dip in rates translates to more affordable monthly payments and a chance to build equity in a growing market.

## Why 2026 is a Golden Opportunity for Southeast Pennsylvania Home Buyers

Contrary to the fear narratives, 2026 is shaping up as an excellent time to buy, particularly with rates at three-year lows around 5.85-6.13%. Home sales are ticking upward as lower rates draw more buyers back, yet competition remains muted compared to the frenzy of low-rate years. In Southeast PA, neighborhoods in Bucks County or Montgomery County offer strong appreciation potential, with prices holding firm due to low inventory but not skyrocketing uncontrollably.

Financial advisors from independent outlets stress that even in high-rate eras, homeownership builds wealth over time, outperforming stocks and bonds in stable inflation environments. If you’re ready financially, don’t wait for Fed cuts or mythical “perfect” conditions—act now to secure a property in this desirable region. The forex market enters 2026 amid heightened volatility driven by U.S. policy shifts, geopolitical flashpoints, and divergent central bank paths.

As of January 22, 2026, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) hovers around 98.6 after dipping 0.16% today, reflecting relief from eased Greenland tensions following President Trump's announcement of a framework deal and tariff rollback on European imports.

Major pairs show mixed dynamics: EUR/USD consolidates above 1.17 after a bullish rebound from tariff fears, USD/JPY remains attractive for yen weakness plays near recent highs, and [GBP/USD](https://www.xtb.com/int/forex) faces chop around 1.35-1.37 levels. Broader themes include potential Fed dovishness under Trump influence, tariff risks as negotiation tools, and safe-haven flows amid Venezuela raids and Iran protests.

In this in-depth analysis, we examine the forex market's current situation, key drivers for 2026 (policy, geopolitics, rates), major pair breakdowns, valuation/technical insights, risks, and trading outlook for the year.

#### 1. Current Forex Market Situation (as of January 22, 2026)

After a turbulent start to the year, forex has stabilized:

DXY: ~98.6 (down modestly today on de-escalation; up 0.68% monthly but -8.74% YoY).

EUR/USD: ~1.1714 (bullish consolidation post-tariff relief; testing triangle breakout near 1.1760 resistance).

GBP/USD: ~1.35-1.37 range (volatility from UK positioning; struggling at 1.35 psychological level).

USD/JPY: Near highs (yen weakness dominant; crosses like EUR/JPY/GBP/JPY in bull flags/breakouts).

USD/CAD: Rebounding after sharp selloff (bulls regaining control post-Trump remarks).

Other Notables: AUD/USD/NZD/USD in focus for commodity ties; USD/CHF eyeing bearish breakdown.

Markets rebounded sharply January 21 on Trump's Greenland de-escalation, with equities up and dollar softening on reduced safe-haven demand. PCE inflation data today and upcoming Fed decisions add layers.

#### 2. Key Drivers for Forex in 2026

Forex is shaped by macro/policy divergence and geopolitical risks:

A. U.S. Policy & Fed Outlook Trump's influence pushes for dovish Fed (potential chair replacement), with bets on more cuts despite solid data (Q3 GDP revised to 4.4%). This supports dollar weakness long-term, though near-term strength from growth/yields persists.

B. Trump Tariffs as Negotiation Tool Threats (e.g., Greenland/Europe) triggered "Sell America" trades and euro strength, but de-escalations ease pressure. Tariffs remain a wildcard for inflation and trade flows.

C. Geopolitical Flashpoints [Venezuela](https://www.bbntimes.com/global-economy/marco-rubio-insists-no-war-with-venezuela-as-ousted-leader-maduro-held-in-new-york-jail) raid, Iran protests, and Greenland crisis spiked oil/safe-haven demand early January, but limited disruption so far. Russia-Ukraine and Middle East add risk premiums.

D. Central Bank Divergence Fed vs. ECB/BoE/BoJ: ECB/BoE more cautious, BoJ normalizing slowly—favoring USD vs. JPY, but rotation into EUR/GBP on U.S. moderation.

#### 3. Major Forex Pairs Landscape in 2026

Key pairs reflect themes of dollar rotation and yen weakness.

#### 4. Valuation & Technical Analysis: Are Majors Cheap or Expensive?

EUR/USD: Bullish from 200-DMA support (~1.16); triangle breakout targets 1.1919 high. Support at 1.1625-1.17.

GBP/USD: Range-bound; 1.35 resistance key. Upside to 1.3725 if breaks.

Analyst Consensus Targets: EUR/USD ~1.19-1.22 (J.P. Morgan/MUFG); USD/JPY ~139-158; overall modest USD decline (~5%) but rotation favors non-USD.

Technicals favor bullish EUR crosses and USD/JPY upside, with DXY overvalued structurally.

#### 5. Risks to Watch in 2026

Policy Uncertainty: Fed independence threats, dovish tilt.

Tariff Escalation: Renewed threats could spike volatility/inflation.

Geopolitics: Venezuela/Iran/[Middle East](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world/middle_east) disruptions; Greenland follow-up.

Data/Events: PCE today, payrolls, central bank meetings.

Intervention: BoJ on yen; carry unwind risks.

#### 6. Analyst Views & Forecasts

Consensus leans toward modest USD weakness long-term (MUFG ~5% decline), but near-term strength in select pairs (USD/JPY). Bullish on EUR/USD rotation; cautious on GBP. Overall: Moderate Buy on non-USD majors for diversification.

#### Conclusion: Navigating Forex in a Policy-Driven Year

Forex in 2026 is defined by U.S. policy unpredictability, geopolitical noise, and central bank divergence. Early-year volatility from Greenland/Venezuela/Iran has eased, allowing rebounds, but risks linger. Structural dollar overvaluation suggests rotation opportunities, especially in EUR/USD and yen crosses.

**A new analysis from Coin Metrics, authored by Senior Research Associate Tanay Ved, finds that January’s record $8 trillion in adjusted [stablecoin](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-are-stablecoins/ "Learn about Stablecoins") transfer [volume](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-trading-volume/ "Learn about Trading Volume") was largely driven by USDC activity on Base, with much of the spike tied to [decentralized finance](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-defi-decentralized-finance/ "Learn about Decentralized Finance (DeFi)") ( [DeFi](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-defi-decentralized-finance/ "Learn about Decentralized Finance (DeFi)")) mechanics rather than payments.**

## Tanay Ved of Coin Metrics Breaks Down USDC’s $5.3T Month on Base

Coin Metrics [reported](https://coinmetrics.substack.com/p/state-of-the-network-issue-351) that adjusted [stablecoin](https://news.bitcoin.com/what-are-stablecoins-a-simple-explanation-of-the-digital-asset-bridging-crypto-and-fiat/) transfer [volume](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-trading-volume/ "Learn about Trading Volume") reached a record $8 trillion in January 2026, with the bulk of growth concentrated in USDC on Base. The report, titled “*The Curious Case of USDC on Base*,” and authored by [Tanay Ved](https://x.com/TanayVed), Senior Research Associate at [Coin Metrics](https://coinmetrics.io), attributes much of the expansion to activity on a single asset and network combination.

According to Coin Metrics Network Data Pro, USDC on Base, with roughly $4.1 billion in supply, generated approximately $5.3 trillion in transaction [volume](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-trading-volume/ "Learn about Trading Volume") in January alone. The company’s senior researcher notes that this translates into unusually high velocity compared with other chains, prompting closer inspection of the underlying drivers.

Coin Metrics data show that the increase was dominated by large transfers. Daily USDC transactions above $100,000 on Base climbed from fewer than 50,000 in mid-2025 to more than 450,000 at peak levels in January 2026. The report shows that transfers between $100,000 and $10 million accounted for roughly 90% of total transfer value, while the largest bands, above $10 million, spiked intermittently.

To determine the source of this activity, the Coin Metrics analyst used ATLAS data to analyze USDC balance updates on Base during a concentrated 10-day window in January. The top five addresses were linked to [DeFi](https://news.bitcoin.com/unlocking-the-future-your-fun-guide-to-decentralized-finance-and-web3/) infrastructure, particularly [liquidity](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-liquidity/ "Learn about Liquidity") provision on Aerodrome and lending and flash loan activity on [Morpho](https://news.bitcoin.com/morpho-association-and-apollo-sign-cooperation-agreement/).

Coin Metrics ATLAS data show that Aerodrome’s WETH/USDC concentrated [liquidity pool](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-are-liquidity-pools/ "Learn about Liquidity Pools") alone accounted for an estimated 32%, or $6.4 trillion, of all USDC adjusted transfer value on Base over the past year. Combined with Aerodrome’s cbBTC/USDC pool and Morpho activity, these contracts represented a substantial share of flows tied to [DeFi](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-defi-decentralized-finance/ "Learn about Decentralized Finance (DeFi)") mechanics rather than traditional payments.

The analysis explains that concentrated [liquidity](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-liquidity/ "Learn about Liquidity") models or providers incentivize frequent rebalancing. As price ranges shift, [liquidity](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-liquidity/ "Learn about Liquidity") providers (LPs) withdraw and redeploy USDC, generating large inflows and outflows with limited net change to pool balances. At peak levels in January, the WETH/USDC pool recorded over $100 billion in daily USDC transfer [volume](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-trading-volume/ "Learn about Trading Volume"), while daily net flows typically remained within $20 million.

Coin Metrics also identifies flash loan activity on Morpho as another major contributor. A single flash loan transaction involving $114 million in USDC illustrates how bots borrow and repay large sums within one atomic transaction, creating significant transfer [volume](http://www.bitcoin.com/get-started/what-is-trading-volume/ "Learn about Trading Volume") without representing net economic movement.

# Warren Buffett: Beware The Investment Activity That Produces Applause

Johnny HopkinsFebruary 18, 2026[Warren Buffett](https://acquirersmultiple.com/category/warren-buffett/ "View all posts in: “Warren Buffett\”")[Leave a Comment](https://acquirersmultiple.com/2026/02/warren-buffett-beware-the-investment-activity-that-produces-applause/#respond "Leave a comment on: “Warren Buffett: Beware The Investment Activity That Produces Applause\”")

![](https://acquirersmultiple.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/buffett-846x846.png)

# 

![](https://acquirersmultiple.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/ambook.jpg)

Market volatility often pushes investors toward emotional decisions, yet Warren Buffett’s 2008 shareholder commentary offers enduring perspective on discipline, valuation, and temperament. His observations during the financial crisis remain relevant for equity investors weighing risk, sentiment, and long-term positioning.

Buffett captured the psychological edge required in uncertain markets with a simple reminder: “When investing, pessimism is your friend, euphoria the enemy.”

That framing reflects a recurring pattern in capital markets. Periods of fear frequently produce attractive entry points, while widespread optimism can inflate valuations beyond fundamentals.

Investors who maintain liquidity and patience during downturns are often positioned to deploy capital when opportunities are most compelling.

Valuation discipline sits at the core of that approach. Buffett reiterated a principle rooted in classic value investing: “Price is what you pay; value is what you get.”

The distinction becomes critical when headlines dominate decision-making. A falling share price does not automatically signal deteriorating intrinsic value, just as a rising market does not guarantee durable earnings power.

Careful analysis of balance sheets, cash flows, and competitive positioning remains essential regardless of macro noise.

Another behavioral trap Buffett highlighted involves the desire for consensus validation. He wrote, “Approval, though, is not the goal of investing.” Investors frequently seek reassurance from media narratives or peer positioning, yet markets reward independent analysis rather than popularity.

Following the crowd can reduce psychological discomfort, but it often limits upside and increases exposure to speculative excess.

This leads directly to Buffett’s caution about market reactions: “Beware the investment activity that produces applause; the great moves are usually greeted by yawns.”

Historically, many of the most successful long-term allocations were initially viewed as unremarkable or even questionable. Contrarian positioning requires conviction grounded in research rather than short-term validation.

Fixed-income positioning during crises also drew his attention. Buffett observed, “Clinging to cash equivalents or long-term government bonds at present yields is almost certainly a terrible policy if continued for long.”

While capital preservation has a role, excessively defensive allocations can erode purchasing power and reduce participation in eventual recoveries. Balanced portfolios that incorporate equities, productive assets, and reasonable liquidity often provide better long-run outcomes.

For investors evaluating current conditions, the broader takeaway centers on temperament. Market cycles inevitably bring dislocation, but disciplined investors focus on valuation, earnings durability, and capital allocation rather than headlines.

Buffett’s crisis-era reflections emphasize patience, rationality, and skepticism toward consensus enthusiasm—principles that remain central to navigating evolving equity markets.

# Arthur Hayes: Bitcoin Will Hit New Highs After AI-Driven Credit Crisis

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes argues Bitcoin's crash from its $126,000 peak signals an AI-driven credit crisis, but predicts the Fed's response will push BTC to new records.

![Arthur Hayes Bitcoin analysis concept showing AI and credit markets convergence with cryptocurrency charts](/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fnews%2Farthur-hayes-ai-credit-crisis-bitcoin-new-highs.webp&w=3840&q=75&dpl=dpl_Hy5n74riM7P3EV48493wqmh47QqE)

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes says Bitcoin's 47% decline from its $126,000 peak is a "fiat liquidity fire alarm," and the worst may still come before the biggest rally.

## What Happened

In a new essay titled "This Is Fine," published February 18, Arthur Hayes laid out a thesis that Bitcoin's sharp decline from its October 2025 all-time high of $126,000 is not random market turbulence. It is a signal. While the Nasdaq has remained relatively flat during the same period, Bitcoin has diverged sharply downward, a pattern Hayes interprets as the market pricing in deflationary stress that traditional indices have not yet acknowledged.

Hayes models a scenario in which artificial intelligence displaces roughly 20% of America's 72.1 million knowledge workers. In his framework, that level of displacement would trigger approximately $557 billion in consumer credit and mortgage defaults, roughly half the severity of the 2008 financial crisis. The resulting wave of bank failures, particularly among regional lenders, would force the Federal Reserve into what Hayes calls "the biggest money printing in history."

## Why It Matters

Hayes's thesis matters because it connects two dominant narratives, the AI boom and the crypto crash, into a single macro framework. His argument is that Bitcoin functions as a leading indicator for dollar liquidity conditions, and that its current decline reflects tightening that equities have not yet priced in.

If Hayes is right, the path forward follows a familiar pattern from 2023: a credit shock forces the Fed to inject emergency liquidity, and Bitcoin rallies as the market prices in sustained money printing. He points to the March 2023 regional bank crisis, when the Fed's intervention triggered a BTC rally of over 40% in the following months, as a template for what comes next.

Hayes warned, however, that Bitcoin could fall further before the Fed acts, potentially breaking below $60,000 as political inertia delays the central bank's response. In the short term, that creates more pain for holders already dealing with four consecutive weeks of ETF outflows totaling $3.8 billion.

## What to Watch

The key variable is timing. Hayes does not predict when AI-driven layoffs will reach critical mass, but he argues the credit deterioration is already underway. Traders should watch regional bank earnings, consumer credit delinquency rates, and any shift in Fed language toward emergency measures. If the Fed signals a return to quantitative easing or launches a new lending facility, Hayes expects Bitcoin to "pump decisively off its lows" and move toward new all-time highs.

### Key Takeaways

Hayes's analysis is a contrarian bet in a deeply bearish market. Whether his AI credit crisis scenario plays out or not, his framework offers a clear set of signals to monitor. For now, Bitcoin remains caught between macro fear and the potential for a liquidity-driven reversal.

## Digital asset outflows extend to 4Th week amid US weakness, selective altcoin resilience

Fourth consecutive week of outflows, totalling US$173M, with US$3.74B withdrawn over the past 4 weeks.

Sharp regional divergence, with US$403M in US outflows offset by US$230M of inflows across Europe and Canada

Bitcoin and Ethereum led outflows, while XRP and Solana continued to attract fresh inflows

Digital asset investment products saw a fourth consecutive week of outflows totalling US$173m, bringing the cumulative four-week run of outflows to US$3.74B. The week began on a more positive note, with inflows of US$575M, followed by outflows of US$853M, likely driven by further price weakness. Sentiment improved slightly on Friday following weaker than expected CPI data, with inflows of US$105M. ETP trading volumes fell markedly to US$27B, down from the record US$63B the prior week.

![Weekly crypto asset flows 16022026](https://a.storyblok.com/f/176807/1600x1200/b1932028c1/weekly-crypto-asset-flows-16022026.png/m/)Regional flows marked a significant divergence in sentiment between the US and the rest of the world. The US saw US$403M in outflows, while all other regions recorded inflows totalling US$230M, most notably Germany at US$115M, Canada at US$46.3M and Switzerland at US$36.8M.

![Weekly crypto asset flows 16022026](https://a.storyblok.com/f/176807/1600x1200/b1932028c1/weekly-crypto-asset-flows-16022026.png/m/)

![Flows by exchange country 16022026](https://a.storyblok.com/f/176807/1600x2000/65d51d25f9/flows-by-exchange-country-16022026.png/m/)Bitcoin saw the weakest sentiment, with US$133M in outflows, although short Bitcoin investment products also recorded outflows, now totalling US$15.4M over the past two weeks, a pattern often seen near market lows.

![Flows by exchange country 16022026](https://a.storyblok.com/f/176807/1600x2000/65d51d25f9/flows-by-exchange-country-16022026.png/m/)

Ethereum also suffered, with US$85.1M in outflows, as did Hyperliquid, which saw US$1M in outflows.

Sentiment remained buoyant for XRP, Solana and Chainlink, which saw inflows of US$33.4M, US$31M and US$1.1M respectively last week.
